title: Stream span anchoring and sensitive segment gating playbook
creator: Priya Kannan
description: Implement a robust playbook for per-segment telemetry that anchors tracing spans to incremental output boundaries while enforcing selective egress policies for sensitive content. This work covers three coordinated areas: (1) span anchoring: emit lightweight span anchors at deterministic segment boundaries so downstream traces can stitch incremental outputs without duplicating PII; (2) sensitive segment gating: attach segment-level sensitivity flags computed by the runtime (heuristic + ML classifier) and use them to gate metrics/logs exported to downstream sinks; (3) compatibility shim: provide a compatibility layer for older SDKs and webhook consumers so they can interpret anchored span events and sensitivity markers without changing contracts. Goals: preserve end-to-end traceability for streamed responses, prevent accidental PII leakage in logs/metrics, and keep overhead <2% p99 latency for standard gen requests.

notes: Decision: use deterministic token-window anchors aligned with batching to simplify reassembly and reduce exporter noise.
Trade-off: classifier on-device reduces exported PII but may miss edge-case sensitive tokens; we will iterate thresholds from telemetry and a curated prompt set.
Fallback policy: if compatibility header present, runtime emits legacy-span-link events instead of anchors to preserve older consumer expectations.
Follow-ups: metrics filter rules for Datadog/Prometheus exporters and an egress allowlist for third-party sinks. Also add canary with sampling=1% across top 10 customers before broad rollout.
